verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents two first-party rule engines. Runbooks evaluate conditions whenever an incident is declared and trigger actions such as Slack channels, Zoom meetings and outbound webhooks. Signals Alert Rules match incoming events, turn them into alerts and route them via escalation policies, with CEL backtesting. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of rule-triggered automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
Teams configure Alert Triggers (see next section) to describe which events should alert and whom, and when a Rule matches, the Event is turned into an Alert and routed to the relevant party
Some examples of actions include creating a Slack channel, starting a Zoom meeting
FireHydrant enables you to create webhooks that respond to internal events or custom commands to send information to external systems.
